title: Eshelby uniformity: existence, rigidity, and stability
editorial_status: Source-checked family; formulation review varies by record
summary: Which inclusion shapes produce uniform interior strain, when does uniformity determine the shape, and how does approximate uniformity constrain departures from those shapes?

statement.lead: Fix the body, constitutive tensor, interface, outer boundary condition, and nonzero constant eigenstrain. Seek an inclusion and an unknown constant interior strain.
statement.after: Existence asks whether such shapes occur; rigidity asks which shapes are forced by uniformity; stability asks what approximate uniformity implies. State separately one, several, or all eigenstrain modes.

why: Uniform inclusion fields underpin micromechanical models of precipitates, transformations, and composites.
Outer boundaries and interactions can change both the exact uniformity family and the validity of an ellipsoidal approximation.
Rigidity and quantitative stability distinguish geometric identification from approximation error control.
scope: Linear elasticity; the classical infinite homogeneous isotropic 3D body is the baseline.
Each subproblem fixes dimension, loading quantifier, moduli, interface, boundary condition, and admissible shape class.
Established baselines, partial theorems, numerical constructions, and formulations under review are separately labeled.

boundary.text: Eshelby’s ellipsoid has spatially constant interior strain for any constant eigenstrain. The same shape works for all such eigenstrains, although the constant response changes with the imposed tensor.

Dai, Ru and Gao construct non-elliptical shapes in the anti-plane eigenstrain problem using an analytic formulation and numerical examples. Antipov treats a related anti-plane inhomogeneity/loading problem. Neither is the coupled plane-strain problem.

Lu, Zhang and Dai derive necessary restrictions for plane deformation. Their Eqs. (48)–(49) constrain the eigenstrain and proposed constant stress; satisfying these conditions does not establish existence.

Full-space ellipsoidal uniformity supplies the reference. Half-space field solvers, including Esh3D, evaluate the response of prescribed inclusions; they do not establish inverse existence of an exactly uniform bounded shape.
Dai’s circular-host anti-plane study gives a necessary-and-sufficient infinite system and numerical solutions of its truncations. It does not prove existence for the present 3D problem.

Zou and He solve the eccentric-sphere forward problem. Wang and Schiavone’s 2026 circular-inclusion study gives finite-domain 2D forward solutions. These fixed-shape calculations are benchmarks, not inverse existence theorems.
A separate 2026 concentric-sphere result restores uniformity by tuning a Steigmann–Ogden interface. That changes the interface law rather than solving the perfect-bonding shape-only problem.

Periodic E-inclusions are constructed through an obstacle problem. The scalar constant-Hessian property gives a hydrostatic elastic construction; the extension to arbitrary elastic modes has additional constitutive restrictions.
Liu’s 2D result excludes symmetric non-dilatational uniformity for a Vigdergauz structure unless it degenerates to a laminate. This is not a 3D classification theorem.

The weak three-dimensional Eshelby conjecture is established by Kang and Milton; Liu develops the associated potential-theory formulations. In this classical all-loadings setting, uniformity characterizes ellipsoids.

Ammari et al. prove single-loading results when the constant interior strain has all equal or all distinct eigenvalues, and a two-loading result. Yuan et al. formulate the residual eigenstress case and obtain necessary conditions and constrained characterizations.

Yuan et al.’s Theorem 3.2 uses the same eigenstress with two linearly independent isotropic tensors; Theorem 3.3 adds an ellipsoid-matched field condition. These do not complete the one-fixed-material statement.

Ni’s preprint reports local two-sided geometry-only stability at the half-order Sobolev scale, a sphere spectrum, and a separate convergent residual-field enclosure for prescribed finite shapes, with independently assembled FEM comparisons.
boundary.evidence_type: Preprint theorem claims and numerical evidence

boundary.text: Half-plane, periodic, and finite-domain constructions show that the exact family and its loading dependence change with the setting. The full-space stability preprint does not establish stability for these families.

settle: Use each subproblem’s settlement criterion; existence, rigidity, and stability are not interchangeable.

progress.title: Necessary restrictions for plane-deformation half-plane uniformity
progress.text: Lu, Zhang and Dai establish necessary conditions for a fixed flat free surface. These restrict admissible eigenstrain/stress pairs without proving universal nonexistence or existence of the exceptional cases.

progress.title: Interface compensation in a finite concentric spherical domain
progress.text: Wang and Schiavone obtain a uniformity condition involving a Steigmann–Ogden interface under free or clamped outer conditions. This is a distinct imperfect-interface model.

progress.title: Preprint available: local stability and convergent finite-shape bounds
progress.text: The arXiv preprint reports nonlinear two-sided local stability, the critical half-order geometric scale with an exact sphere spectrum, and convergent bounds for prescribed finite geometries. Independent displacement-based finite-element comparisons provide numerical evidence. EL01 now distinguishes these results from the remaining global geometry-only and broader physical-setting questions.

progress.title: Local nonlinear two-sided stability assembled
progress.text: The current study develops a manuscript-stage local theorem around general nondegenerate ellipsoids in the homogeneous-isotropic dilatational setting.

progress.title: Finite-shape enclosure and independent FEM comparison
progress.text: A complementary shape-specific residual-field enclosure was paired with an independently assembled displacement-based elasticity calculation.

subproblems.title: Classical ellipsoids in an infinite 3D body
subproblems.problem_statement: Which shapes are known to produce exactly uniform interior strain for every constant eigenstrain in the classical infinite-body setting?
subproblems.why_it_matters: This is the reference solution behind ellipsoidal models of precipitates, transforming regions, and dilute composites.
subproblems.model_and_scope: An infinite 3D homogeneous isotropic linear-elastic body; identical inclusion and matrix moduli, perfect bonding, one bounded ellipsoid, constant eigenstrain, and no remote loading. The elastic strain decays at infinity.

known_results.text: Eshelby’s ellipsoid has spatially constant interior strain for any constant eigenstrain. The same shape works for all such eigenstrains, although the constant response changes with the imposed tensor.

subproblems.what_remains_open: Existence in this setting is established. Shape characterization belongs to R0/R1; robustness and changes of boundary conditions belong to the other records.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: The classical forward construction settles this baseline. An extension must specify the changed material, interface, loading, or outer boundary.
subproblems.progress_and_sources: Classical result (1957); included as the starting point, not as a newly open problem.

subproblems.title: Uniformity near a flat free boundary: anti-plane and plane strain
subproblems.problem_statement: For a prescribed nonzero in-plane eigenstrain, can a buried inclusion in a traction-free isotropic half-plane have exactly uniform interior strain?
subproblems.why_it_matters: A nearby surface interacts with a transforming region and can invalidate the isolated-ellipsoid approximation.
subproblems.model_and_scope: Plane strain, equal positive-definite isotropic moduli, perfect bonding, a fixed straight traction-free edge, no external loading, and a smooth simply connected inclusion with fixed area and centroid depth and positive edge clearance. The constant interior strain is an unknown, not an additional prescribed datum.

known_results.text: Dai, Ru and Gao construct non-elliptical shapes in the anti-plane eigenstrain problem using an analytic formulation and numerical examples. Antipov treats a related anti-plane inhomogeneity/loading problem. Neither is the coupled plane-strain problem.

Lu, Zhang and Dai derive necessary restrictions for plane deformation. Their Eqs. (48)–(49) constrain the eigenstrain and proposed constant stress; satisfying these conditions does not establish existence.

subproblems.what_remains_open: Determine whether the admissible cases actually support exact shapes, or prove nonexistence for a stated eigenstrain and shape class. The 2026 restrictions do not by themselves exclude every possible constant interior response.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: An exact admissible shape and verified field, a rigorous existence theorem, or a nonexistence theorem with the loading and geometric hypotheses explicit. A small numerical residual alone is insufficient.
subproblems.scientific_status: Necessary conditions; existence formulation under review
subproblems.progress_and_sources: 2015/2021 anti-plane constructions and the 2026 plane-deformation restrictions are recorded separately.

subproblems.title: A bounded inclusion in a 3D half-space
subproblems.problem_statement: For fixed isotropic moduli and a prescribed nonzero constant eigenstrain, does a bounded inclusion below a flat free surface admit exact interior uniformity?
subproblems.why_it_matters: This is the fully three-dimensional surface-interaction question for particles and transforming zones.
subproblems.model_and_scope: A homogeneous isotropic 3D half-space with positive-definite elasticity, equal moduli, perfect bonding, zero surface traction, no remote load, and decay at infinity. Seek a smooth bounded simply connected inclusion at fixed volume and centroid depth with positive surface clearance. Cylinders extending infinitely in one direction are excluded.

known_results.text: Full-space ellipsoidal uniformity supplies the reference. Half-space field solvers, including Esh3D, evaluate the response of prescribed inclusions; they do not establish inverse existence of an exactly uniform bounded shape.

subproblems.what_remains_open: The checked sources do not settle this precise shape-only existence question. Anti-plane examples and finite-order perturbative cancellation cannot be promoted to a bounded 3D construction.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: Construct one exact bounded example for specified data, or prove exclusion for an explicit loading and admissible class. Classification across eigenstrain modes would be a broader result.
subproblems.scientific_status: No resolution identified in sources checked
subproblems.progress_and_sources: Literature checked on 10 November 2026; the absence of an identified result is not certification of global openness.

subproblems.title: Shape compensation in a fixed finite body
subproblems.problem_statement: Can inclusion shape alone restore exact uniformity in a fixed finite 3D host, for a traction-free boundary or a rigidly clamped boundary?
subproblems.why_it_matters: Finite specimens and particles near external boundaries require a theory that retains the outer geometry.
subproblems.model_and_scope: Use a fixed spherical host, prescribed nonzero constant eigenstrain, equal positive-definite isotropic moduli, and perfect bonding. Fix inclusion volume and a noncentral centroid, with positive boundary clearance. Treat zero traction and zero displacement as separate problems; remove rigid motions in the traction case.

known_results.text: Dai’s circular-host anti-plane study gives a necessary-and-sufficient infinite system and numerical solutions of its truncations. It does not prove existence for the present 3D problem.

Zou and He solve the eccentric-sphere forward problem. Wang and Schiavone’s 2026 circular-inclusion study gives finite-domain 2D forward solutions. These fixed-shape calculations are benchmarks, not inverse existence theorems.
A separate 2026 concentric-sphere result restores uniformity by tuning a Steigmann–Ogden interface. That changes the interface law rather than solving the perfect-bonding shape-only problem.

subproblems.what_remains_open: Establish existence or nonexistence for each fixed outer boundary condition. Centered hydrostatic spheres, tailored outer tractions, and jointly designed host/interface geometries answer different questions.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: An exact construction or a rigorous obstruction with host, position, volume, eigenstrain, and boundary condition held fixed.
subproblems.progress_and_sources: The 2023 anti-plane criterion and 2017/2026 forward and interface results delimit the proposed question.

subproblems.title: Periodic uniformity for more than one eigenstrain mode
subproblems.problem_statement: Can one isolated inclusion in a fixed 3D periodic cell have uniform interior strain for both a prescribed dilatational mode and an independent prescribed deviatoric mode?
subproblems.why_it_matters: A useful inclusion idealization for dense composites must account for interactions and the loading modes it supports.
subproblems.model_and_scope: Fix the lattice, volume fraction, equal positive-definite isotropic moduli, and perfect bonding. Require a smooth connected inclusion compactly inside the cell, periodic displacement with zero mean, and zero average total strain. Apply the two nonzero constant eigenstrains in separate tests to the same shape; exclude laminates and cell-spanning phases.

known_results.text: Periodic E-inclusions are constructed through an obstacle problem. The scalar constant-Hessian property gives a hydrostatic elastic construction; the extension to arbitrary elastic modes has additional constitutive restrictions.
Liu’s 2D result excludes symmetric non-dilatational uniformity for a Vigdergauz structure unless it degenerates to a laminate. This is not a 3D classification theorem.

subproblems.what_remains_open: Determine compatibility of the two prescribed modes in this isolated 3D class. A scalar E-inclusion result alone does not settle it; the exact literature boundary remains under review.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: Prove simultaneous uniformity for both separate tests on an admissible shape, or a no-go theorem for the stated mode pair and class.
subproblems.scientific_status: Single-mode constructions; multimode formulation under review
subproblems.progress_and_sources: The 2007 article, 2010 periodic analysis, and later arXiv copy of the detailed E-inclusion manuscript are distinguished by publication record.

subproblems.title: The all-loadings converse in infinite 3D space
subproblems.problem_statement: If a fixed inclusion has uniform interior strain for every constant eigenstrain, must it be an ellipsoid?
subproblems.why_it_matters: This determines when uniformity identifies the geometry rather than merely providing an example.
subproblems.model_and_scope: Classical homogeneous isotropic 3D full space with positive-definite moduli, perfect bonding, no remote load, and a bounded smooth simply connected inclusion. Keep the material tensor and inclusion fixed while varying the constant symmetric eigenstrain.

known_results.text: The weak three-dimensional Eshelby conjecture is established by Kang and Milton; Liu develops the associated potential-theory formulations. In this classical all-loadings setting, uniformity characterizes ellipsoids.

subproblems.what_remains_open: This baseline is settled. Replacing all eigenstrains by one, changing the boundary, or changing the constitutive model requires a separate statement.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: The established converse settles the stated baseline. Any extension must retain its own loading quantifiers and material assumptions.
subproblems.progress_and_sources: Classical converse results (2008); retained separately from the single-loading frontier.

subproblems.title: Single-loading rigidity and the repeated-eigenvalue case
subproblems.problem_statement: For one fixed physical isotropic material tensor and a nonzero eigenstress with exactly two equal eigenvalues, does uniform interior strain force a bounded inclusion to be ellipsoidal?
subproblems.why_it_matters: A single transformation or loading is the experimentally natural inverse test, but it contains less information than all loadings.
subproblems.model_and_scope: Infinite homogeneous isotropic 3D space, positive-definite elasticity, perfect bonding, a connected bounded Lipschitz inclusion, and eigenstress C:E* fixed throughout. State convexity whenever used. Do not replace one fixed material by simultaneous tests in two materials.

known_results.text: Ammari et al. prove single-loading results when the constant interior strain has all equal or all distinct eigenvalues, and a two-loading result. Yuan et al. formulate the residual eigenstress case and obtain necessary conditions and constrained characterizations.

Yuan et al.’s Theorem 3.2 uses the same eigenstress with two linearly independent isotropic tensors; Theorem 3.3 adds an ellipsoid-matched field condition. These do not complete the one-fixed-material statement.

subproblems.what_remains_open: Remove the additional constraints in the repeated-eigenvalue formulation, or exhibit a non-ellipsoidal counterexample in the same physical setting. No later complete resolution was identified in this check.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: A proof with the original single-material quantifiers, or a counterexample with exact whole-interior uniformity and all hypotheses verified.
subproblems.progress_and_sources: 2010 and 2023 results are recorded with their distinct strain/eigenstress variables and extra hypotheses.

subproblems.title: Quantitative stability in infinite 3D space
subproblems.problem_statement: How does whole-interior strain heterogeneity control, and depend on, the distance of an imperfect inclusion from the ellipsoid family?
subproblems.why_it_matters: This gives an error estimate for replacing a measured microstructure by an ellipsoid and identifies the geometric wavelengths that matter.
subproblems.model_and_scope: The current preprint treats uniform dilatational eigenstrain in an infinite homogeneous isotropic solid, equal moduli, perfect bonding, and no remote loading. The nonlinear two-sided theorem is local near a fixed nondegenerate ellipsoid; the residual-field construction concerns prescribed finite shapes.

known_results.text: Ni’s preprint reports local two-sided geometry-only stability at the half-order Sobolev scale, a sphere spectrum, and a separate convergent residual-field enclosure for prescribed finite shapes, with independently assembled FEM comparisons.
known_results.evidence_type: Preprint theorem claims and numerical evidence

subproblems.what_remains_open: A global geometry-only law, its admissible shape class and metric, effective aspect-ratio dependence, and extensions to other modes and physical settings remain distinct from the available local theorem and finite-shape enclosure.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: Prove a suitably scoped bound or produce a sharp counterexample; report geometric normalization, norms, constants, and independent numerical checks where computation is used.
subproblems.editorial_status: Source-checked preprint; no independent proof certification
subproblems.progress_and_sources: The original EL01 v1.1 stability statement, equations, and history are retained below. arXiv v2 was checked on 10 November 2026.

subproblems.title: Stability with boundaries, interfaces, or periodicity
subproblems.problem_statement: When exact uniform shapes exist in a specified boundary-value problem, does near-uniformity force proximity to that exact family?
subproblems.why_it_matters: Robustness is meaningful only relative to the shapes and constraints of the actual specimen or periodic cell.
subproblems.model_and_scope: Choose one established exact family with fixed moduli, eigenstrain modes, interface law, boundary data, volume, and position constraints. Specify the shape topology and quotient only genuine symmetries. Use that exact family, which need not consist of ellipsoids.

known_results.text: Half-plane, periodic, and finite-domain constructions show that the exact family and its loading dependence change with the setting. The full-space stability preprint does not establish stability for these families.

subproblems.what_remains_open: Identify a quantitative relation between heterogeneity and distance to an established exact family. If the family is empty, a positive minimum heterogeneity requires a normalized compact class and continuity; nonexistence alone is insufficient.
subproblems.settlement_criterion: A two-sided estimate or failure example with explicit norms and constants. For an empty-family lower bound, rule out shrinking, escape to infinite depth, vanishing gaps, and shape degeneration as appropriate.
subproblems.scientific_status: Proposed extension conditional on an exact family
subproblems.progress_and_sources: This is an OPM formulation, not a theorem attributed to the construction papers.

review_note: A focused source and formulation review, not an exhaustive survey or independent verification of every proof. Proposed extensions remain under review. See audit/ESHELBY_FAMILY_2026-11-10.md.
